correctness.rationale: For characteristic two, x+2=x forces first and third characters equal. For odd characteristic p>=5 and q≡1 mod3, expanding the 27-word projector gives constant q; 6 one-supported terms vanish; 12 two-supported terms have Weil bound sqrt(q), 8 three-supported terms bound 2sqrt(q), and three excluded zeros contribute total at most 27. Thus 27N>=q−28sqrt(q)−27>0 for q>=841. The only eligible odd proper prime powers below 841 are exactly q=25,49,121,169,289,343,361,529,625. The actual standalone verifier proves irreducibility of each defining polynomial, independently cross-checks coset colors by cubes and exponentiation, and enumerates every admissible start for all 9. Exactly q25 and q49 fail. All assumptions, ranges and boundaries checked; finite computations are explicitly isolated from the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Simultaneous realization of all 27 ordered cubic-character triples is a natural universality invariant distinct from a monochromatic run. A complete classification across every proper extension q≡1 mod3, with a sharp q=121 transition, two exact small odd-field exceptions, and a characteristic-two obstruction, resolves a motivated finite-field gap left open by a prime-field theorem. This is not merely a new generic Weil bound or an arbitrary sampled slice; the nine finite checks close an infinite theorem and identify its optimal boundary. It does not claim a general frequency formula or priority certainty.
